description:
Export the design you are working on — `format` picks the deliverable: `pdf` (print PDF), `png`/`jpeg`/`webp` (image), `svg` (vector SVG), `pdfx` (print-ready PDF/X), `html` (responsive HTML5), `idml` (Adobe InDesign), `psd` (layered PSD), `mp4` (video), `wav`/`m4a` (audio), `imgly` (editable design file). Renders `blockId` — or the whole document when `blockId` is omitted.

Your edits are saved to the design as you make them (the viewer shows it), so there is nothing to save: every format is a copy for the person — a pdf to print, a png to post, `imgly` the editable design file with its images.

Returns JSON `{ uri, httpUrl, bytes, format }` (plus `path` when you pass `outPath`). `uri` is the durable handle — treat it as opaque and pass it back verbatim where a URI is wanted. `httpUrl` is a fetch link tied to this process — fetch it to download the bytes to disk, or hand it to the user.

`outPath` (optional, absolute path including the filename): ALSO write the artifact to that local path — the workspace copy is still written, and the response then carries `path`. Use it when the file is wanted on disk, and always when your environment cannot fetch localhost URLs (sandboxed harnesses, e.g. Claude Cowork — target your session's outputs folder there).

`format=svg` is the engine's vector export: text is outlined into paths (renders identically everywhere, but is not editable text in the SVG), and raster images are embedded in the file at source resolution — an SVG of a photo-heavy design can be much larger than its source images.

`format=imgly` writes a portable, self-contained `.imgly` design file (scene + all asset bytes bundled) — the inverse of `import`, and the only format that stays editable: a copy to move, back up or send. Whole-design only: `blockId` is not accepted. Because the archive inlines every referenced asset it is the heaviest call this server makes, and it REFUSES rather than ship a design whose fonts or images could not be loaded — retry it, do not ignore it.

`format=pdfx` runs the print PDF through a PDF/X conversion: CMYK with an embedded ICC profile and PDF/X conformance markers, ready for a print shop. Tune it via the optional `pdfx` object — conformance standard (X-4 default / X-3 / X-1a), output profile (fogra39/gracol/srgb/custom), transparency flattening and its resolution, OutputIntent metadata. srgb is never PDF/X compliant. The result carries `warnings` when the file breaks its standard (each names the fix): relay them or re-export before calling the file print-ready. CMYK and spot colours, bleed and the print checklist: `skill://codesign/formats/print.md`.

`format=html` renders ONE page (`blockId` required — pass a page id) to responsive HTML5. Default is a single self-contained `.html` (assets inlined; animated designs get a CDN GSAP player injected so the file plays as-is); `html: { assets: "external" }` delivers html + separate image/font files as one `.zip`.

`format=mp4` renders the authored timeline of the block (typically a page) to an H.264 `mp4`; duration and resolution come from the scene; frame rate is `fps` (default 30). Requires the native engine (the default). Long encodes report MCP progress notifications when the client sends a progressToken. The result also carries `duration` (seconds of video) and `audioDuration` (seconds of audio; absent when the mp4 has no audio track), both read from the encoded file — no need to probe it.

`format=wav` / `format=m4a` renders the audio mix of a page (`blockId` required, a page id): every audio block and video-fill audio on it, over the page duration. `wav` is 48 kHz stereo 16-bit PCM, `m4a` is AAC. The result carries `duration` (seconds, read from the encoded file). To get one clip alone, export while it is the only audio on the page. Requires the native engine. Every clip sounds over exactly its own window (within a few ms), whatever its start and trim. `m4a` as a whole may sit ~35 ms late from AAC encoder priming, as in the mp4.

bleed.description: For `format=png`/`jpeg`/`webp` only (invalid with any other format). A page with print bleed renders trim + bleed by default; `false` renders it at its trim size. The design keeps its bleed.

blockId.description: The page to render; an image format takes any block. Omit to export the whole document: a multi-page PDF, or one composite image of all pages. Required for format=html/psd (pass a page id). Required for `format=mp4` (pass a page id). Required for `format=wav`/`m4a` (pass a page id).

format.description: The deliverable: pdf → print PDF; png/jpeg/webp → image; svg → vector SVG; pdfx → print-ready PDF/X; html → HTML5 page; idml → Adobe InDesign document; psd → layered PSD; mp4 → video; wav/m4a → audio; imgly → editable design file.

fps.description: Frames per second for `format=mp4` only (invalid with any other format), greater than 0. Default: the scene's `scene.frameRate`, which is 30 unless set. Common values: 24, 25, 30, 60.

height.description: For `format=png`/`jpeg`/`webp` only: the image's height in px, scaled up or down; the aspect is kept, and with both the image fits inside them, never stretched. At most 65500 for jpeg and 16383 for webp. Default: the design's own size.

html.description: Options for `format=html` only (invalid with any other format).

assets.description: embedded (default): one self-contained .html, assets inlined as data URLs — viewable anywhere as-is. external: html + separate image/font files, delivered as one .zip.

outPath.description: Absolute path (including filename) to ALSO write the artifact to — the workspace copy is still written, and the response then carries `path`. Use when you need the file on disk and cannot fetch localhost URLs (sandboxed harnesses).

page.description: The page to render by its position in the design, 0 for the first (the order of `engine.scene.getPages()`), instead of its `blockId`. Not with `blockId`, `imgly` or `idml`.

pdfx.description: Options for `format=pdfx` only (invalid with any other format). Omit entirely for sensible print defaults: PDF/X-4, fogra39, embedded ICC.

embedICCProfile.description: Default true. false → plain CMYK (or RGB) PDF with no embedded ICC profile, OutputIntent, or PDF/X markers — for prepress pipelines that apply their own profile.

flattenResolution.description: Dpi of flattened pages, default 300 (PDF/X-1a, and PDF/X-3 unless flattenTransparency is false).

flattenTransparency.description: PDF/X-3 only (default true there): rasterize transparent content for strict compliance. false keeps transparency live — better fidelity, may not validate. Ignored on PDF/X-4; PDF/X-1a always flattens.

nonPrinterProfile.description: Output profile that is not a printer profile (srgb, a custom RGB one): keep (default) writes the file, not compliant; reject fails the export.

outputCondition.description: Overrides /OutputCondition — the human-readable printing-condition description (e.g. "ISO Coated v2 (ECI)"). Defaults from outputProfile.

outputConditionIdentifier.description: Overrides the PDF's /OutputConditionIdentifier — the REGISTERED printing-condition name preflight tools and print shops check (e.g. "FOGRA39", "CGATS 21.2"). Defaults from outputProfile; with a custom profile, your print shop tells you what to put here.

outputProfile.description: Target printing condition / ICC output profile. fogra39 (default) = ISO Coated v2 (ECI), European offset. gracol = GRACoL 2013 CRPC6, US commercial. srgb = keep RGB, for digital distribution — not PDF/X compliant. custom = supply the print shop's ICC file via profileUri.

outputStandard.description: PDF/X conformance target. PDF/X-4 (default) keeps live transparency. PDF/X-3 is the older PDF 1.4 standard — it flattens transparency by default and can rasterize gradients/alpha content. PDF/X-1a: CMYK and spot only (no srgb), always flattened.

profileUri.description: Required with outputProfile="custom" (invalid otherwise): an https:// URL or absolute local file path of the .icc profile to embed.

title.description: PDF document title. Defaults to the design's title.

width.description: For `format=png`/`jpeg`/`webp` only: the image's width in px, scaled up or down; the aspect is kept, and with both the image fits inside them, never stretched. At most 65500 for jpeg and 16383 for webp. Default: the design's own size.

name: export
